title: Campus interest in arranging and the new album's mission
summary: Schools welcome the arranging material now available; the new album is meant to give dedicated young players more to work with.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Okay. Let's see, do you see much emphasis through questions or discussions with people on campuses about composition? Or is it mainly -- do they ask you more about the life of the band, or --

Well, I think it varies, but I think -- I know alone from the arranging aspect of it, that they're certainly making great strides at the high school level and college level of musical instruction. In other words, I find great acceptance from the teaching and people involved in the teaching system, as to the great amount of music that's available now, say, per se, 15 or 20 years ago. There's no comparison in the amount of material and the quality of the material. It's -- this is the one thing that seems to have the best acceptance.
I see. And might hold the most promise.
Now, with the current album that you have, hitting its stride in popularity and so forth, it might be a force in generating that much more interest when you're arriving in campuses now.

That's the whole -- actually, that's the main intent, because no one ever can visualize or predict the sale and the possibilities of financial assistance that you will receive. But we can say that it will do its job as far as

dedicated young players are concerned. It will have more to put their teeth into, and so I feel that these moves are very important. In fact, in this case, we're getting a very good reaction, and I thinkeventually a very good sale makes it even that much more ambitious for me.
But nevertheless, to me the all important thing is that we reach that many more young people.
